violation: The operator key registry is authenticated by the TRANSPORT and by nothing else. GOBLIN-DIV-043 closed the non-member door: raft peers now present verified client certificates in production, so an outsider cannot send InstallSnapshot. A MEMBER still can. Every registry guard - the empty-registry seed rule, the last-key refusal, the prev_serial replay guard, signature verification against replicated key material - runs inside FSM Apply, and InstallSnapshot does not go through Apply. FSM.Restore installs payload.GetOperatorKeys() directly and a snapshot is not a signed object, so a node holding a valid peer certificate can act as leader, forge an FSMSnapshot whose operator_keys map holds its own key, and install it as the cluster's root of trust on every replica in one step. Restore validates each record's derived key id and refuses a mismatch, which keeps the id-is-derived invariant true off the Apply path, but no check inside Restore can distinguish an honest leader's snapshot from a compromised member's - both arrive over an authenticated connection. This is the half of GOBLIN-DIV-043 that transport authentication cannot reach, and it is what still falsifies the piece-1 rationale: 'if any node in the Raft membership could empty and re-seed the registry, node compromise would become operator compromise'. Inside the membership, it does. RESOLVED 2026-08-02. The snapshot now carries the registry's PROVENANCE - the founding OperatorKeySeed and every signed OperatorKeyChange that actually mutated the registry, in apply order - and core/consensus/fsm_snapshot_trust.go replays it on Restore against the keys THIS NODE was configured with via --operator-key. A forger cannot produce the signatures, so it cannot produce a chain that replays; and the replay's output is compared against the registry the snapshot claims, so an honest chain cannot be pasted onto a dishonest result. TWO OPERATOR DECISIONS shaped it, both 2026-08-02. (1) THE ANCHOR IS SET EQUALITY, not intersection. The seed is unsigned - it must be, since it is authorized by the registry being empty and there is no key yet to sign against - which makes it the one link a forger writes freely. Anchoring on 'some key I trust appears in the chain' accepts a forged seed of {honest key, attacker key}: internally consistent, trivially valid, fatal. That is not a theoretical objection; it is a test case, and weakening the anchor makes exactly that case pass and no other. The consequence is that --operator-key now names the cluster's FOUNDING seed, immutable for the cluster's life: the registry rotates freely above it, but a node joining after a rotation is configured with the founding keys, not the current ones. (2) A NODE WITH NO CONFIGURED KEYS REFUSES a non-empty registry rather than adopting one unverified. Only mixed configuration breaks - a cluster where nobody configured a key keeps an empty registry, carries no provenance, and restores exactly as before, which is the documented fail-closed mode. Permissiveness here would have meant an attacker simply targets an unconfigured follower, and the entry could then only narrow, never close. ONE PREDICTED COST DID NOT MATERIALIZE: the entry expected a schema-reset label, but the two new fields are ADDITIVE and buf breaking passes unchanged. The break is behavioural instead - a pre-047 snapshot carrying a registry has no provenance and is refused with the same remedy the pre-schema-reset JSON snapshot gives: wipe the data dir and rejoin.

violation: Phase 2 does not exist. The architecture doc describes six strictly ordered boot phases including 'Phase 2 - Topological parallel start of local agents', and nothing in goblin starts a local agent. Verified by grep: every StartAll and TopologicalSort hit in the tree is under vendor/, with zero goblin-owned callers. The kernel exports both, the kernel's own supervisor uses them, and the orchestrator does not. Meanwhile goblin's TEARDOWN does reach StopAll, through the kernel's SystemShutdown in pid1Completion.complete - goblin stops agents it never started. The consequence is that the Phase 3 network-readiness gate is structurally dead rather than merely disabled by default: its only producer would be a local network agent, nothing starts local agents, and the only path that starts anything is NodeRPC.StartAgentInstance, the cluster RPC the gate is supposed to precede. The documented model is circular as written. Implementing Phase 2 as a literal StartAll was considered and deliberately rejected: discovery registers every agent it finds and enablement defaults to on (only an explicit "enabled": false disables), and nothing distinguishes a boot-local service from a cluster-schedulable template, so a type that is both installed and globally registered would run as the template on every node AND as scheduled instances. Measured blast radius: test/cluster/harness_test.go:80 installs a sleeper fixture and :213 passes its directory to every node as RUNTIME_AGENT_PATH, so a literal StartAll would start a sleeper on every node in every cluster test.
rule: goblin-architecture.md boot phases (six strictly ordered phases; Phase 2 topological start of local agents); cooperative-ecosystem-manifesto (the ledger records the gap, a comment does not)
exit: The selection mechanism is the exit, not the start loop. Systemd-like targets: an agent is boot-local if it is WantedBy a target on the boot path and cluster-schedulable if it is not, so the distinction falls out of the dependency graph instead of being a classification someone invents. wanted_by is ALREADY parsed by the kernel's discovery and consumed by nothing, which is the shape to fix rather than repeat. Note the cost before starting: this is a design cycle, not a patch. The kernel's toposort already implements the two-relation semantics a target engine needs (hard edges order and cycle-reject; soft edges order when satisfiable and drop rather than block when they would cycle) but it lives in the kernel's internal/ tree, so the orchestrator cannot import it - the exported alternative takes an agent map, the wrong type for targets. Making it reachable is a kernel change. Deliberately NOT done in the change that split the supervisor: a target model MOVES Phase 2 rather than filtering it - the gate becomes a target reached and cluster join becomes a target - so building it against the current shape would put it exactly where targets restructure, which is GOBLIN-DIV-046's own argument one level up.

violation: GAPI is a LIBRARY goblin embeds, and it is named all over goblin's operator-facing surface. An operator running goblind has no reason to know the kernel exists, and every one of these tells them - or worse, instructs them to go use it. MEASURED, and each is visible without reading source. (a) HELP TEXT: 'goblind start --help' prints --listen-addr as 'Single control-plane bind address (QUIC; carries GAPI, RPC, Serf, and Raft via ALPN)'. (b) AN ERROR THAT REDIRECTS TO ANOTHER PRODUCT: tui_provider.go returns 'lifecycle operations not supported in cluster mode - use GAPI CLI for agent management', pointing the operator at a binary that is not part of their installation. (c) A DEFAULT PATH THEY MUST CREATE: phase_local.go falls back to /usr/local/bin/gapi-runner, so installing Python agent support means placing a gapi-named binary. (d) LOGS: goblind emits 'close gapi stream failed', 'gapi message too large', 'failed to read gapi payload', 'failed to unmarshal gapi envelope', 'gapi event received', 'register gapi plane' and 'rpc and gapi planes attached to control-plane listener', and runs a tracked loop named 'gapi-accept'. (e) THE MOUNTED SUBTREE: goblinctl mounts gapictl's command tree wholesale under 'goblinctl agent', so that subtree's help text arrives verbatim - 'goblinctl agent ping --help' prints gapictl's Short, 'Ping gapid', naming a binary that is not part of a goblin installation. Anything gapi adds to that tree lands in goblin's help surface without goblin touching a line, so this half cannot be fixed in goblin alone and pairs with GAPI-DIV-061's prose class. NOT IN SCOPE, because they are not operator-facing: Go import aliases (gapicli, gapiconfig, ...), source comments, ledger identifiers, and internal struct fields such as UnifiedController.gapiAddr. The environment namespace is the same defect in a different medium and is tracked separately as GOBLIN-DIV-055, which depends on GAPI-DIV-061. RESOLVED 2026-08-02, and the enumeration in this entry proved ACCURATE - eleven operator-facing strings, all as listed. Two corrections to the fix rather than the measurement. FIRST, (c) the runner default: /usr/local/bin/gapi-runner was not merely badly named, NOTHING PROVISIONS IT - not the NixOS module, not the Magefile, not any document. Replacing it therefore cannot regress a working deployment because none rested on it, and the replacement resolves beside the running binary the way the kernel's own resolvePyRunner does rather than renaming a default that never worked. SECOND, (e) the mounted subtree: this entry recorded that half as unfixable in goblin alone, and it was half right. gapi's own prose had to move first (GAPI-DIV-061), but the remaining gapictl-named EXAMPLES are fixed here, at mount time - internal/cli/cli.go rewrites 'gapictl ' to 'goblinctl ' as each verb is mounted. That is better than editing the kernel's strings: gapictl keeps examples naming gapictl, goblinctl shows examples naming goblinctl, from one definition, and the examples now RUN as printed. gapi's core/product/scan_test.go declares those nine literals as debt 'tracked by GOBLIN-DIV-056'; that declaration's reasoning is now stale and should be reworded on the next gapi change - the literals stay, the debt does not. Prose names the ROLE per the operator's decision: the 'gapi plane' is the agent-event plane multiplexed beside RPC, so it and its loop and its five log lines describe what they carry.

exit: No operator-facing string produced by a goblin binary names gapi. Help text and flag usage describe the transport by what it carries rather than by the library that implements it; the tui error names a goblin verb or states the limitation without redirecting elsewhere; the runner default is goblin-named or resolved rather than hardcoded to a gapi path; and log messages and loop names use goblin's own vocabulary. CLOSES ON: a test that walks goblin's command tree and asserts no cobra Use, Short, Long or flag usage string matches /gapi/i, plus a scan of error and log message literals in internal/ and cmd/ for the same - under 'Full Build and Test'. A one-time cleanup is explicitly NOT a closure: the property decays the moment someone writes the next log line, which is how it got here. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE: reintroduce one flag-usage mention and one log-message mention and show each go red separately. RESIDUALS. (1) A literal scan cannot see a message composed at runtime from a variable, so a formatted string that interpolates a gapi-derived value passes. (2) It cannot see strings that reach the operator from the VENDORED kernel itself - gapi's own log lines and errors surface in goblind's output and are outside goblin's tree entirely, so no goblin-side gate can reach them. That half is GAPI-DIV-061's prose class, filed the same day on the operator's decision that gapi should rewrite its own operator-facing strings to be complete. This entry cannot make goblind's output gapi-free on its own. (3) The version block's 'Runtime Core' row names the embedded kernel by a neutral label rather than as GAPI, and is deliberately left alone - GOBLIN-DIV-052 closed asserting that row exists. CLOSED 2026-08-02 on internal/cli/vendorname_test.go under 'Full Build and Test'. Two gates. The first walks the LIVE COMMAND TREE rather than scanning source, which is what makes it worth having: goblinctl mounts gapictl's whole verb tree, so half the strings an operator reads appear in no goblin file at all, and a source scan of internal/ would have reported this property satisfied while 'goblinctl agent ping --help' printed 'Ping gapid'. The second scans message literals through the AST - not by matching quotes in raw text, which reads COMMENTS and made the comment explaining a removed bad default trip the gate proving it was removed. DEMONSTRATED BY FAILURE, three sabotages, each restored byte-identical: a flag-usage mention, a log-message mention, and removal of the mount-time rebrand, each reddening a gate separately. THE FLAG SABOTAGE FOUND A HOLE IN THE GATE ITSELF and is the reason to write these down. It was caught only by the literal scan, because the tree walk started at goblinctl's package singleton and never built goblind's root - so a gapi-named string arriving from the VENDORED gapicli.RegisterDaemonFlags would have been caught by neither gate, the literal scan being blind to vendor/ and the walk blind to goblind. The walk now constructs both roots. A sabotage that passes is evidence about the gate, not about the code. RESIDUALS. (1) As the entry predicted, a message composed at runtime from a variable is invisible to a literal scan. (2) Strings reaching the operator from the vendored kernel's own logs and errors are outside goblin's tree entirely; GAPI-DIV-061 fixed gapi's prose class, and the command-tree gate now covers the mounted help specifically because it walks the built tree. (3) The version block's 'Runtime Core' row is deliberately untouched, per GOBLIN-DIV-052. (4) One declared exemption survives: rebrandMounted's own search term 'gapictl ', a literal whose purpose is to erase the name; file-scoped, with a stale-entry check that fails if it stops matching - which it already did once, catching an inert second entry in its own list.
